decisions.why: Sensei is a full-bleed 100dvh chat app: almost every pixel is host surface, border or body text. Taking `skin` would have meant owning light/dark correctness for the entire frame in exchange for colouring a sidebar and a link. The app instead defines app-owned `--sensei-*` tokens used only at identity sites (mark, citation link, active chat, viewer bubble, streaming dot) and redefines NOT ONE `--civitai-*` variable, which `src/lib/brand.test.ts` asserts by grepping for an assignment.
decisions.cost: Two values ARE owned in both themes (`--sensei-accent` light/dark), so the dual-theme debt is real but bounded. It is discharged by computing WCAG contrast from the hexes in `index.css` rather than restating the numbers in a comment.

decisions.fork: add a hero band vs none
decisions.why: Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) There is no band to put it in: the app is a fixed-height iframe whose whole vertical budget is the transcript, and a hero would take rows from the thing the app is FOR — the rubric's own first IA rule. (2) A chat app is re-entered constantly; art that is pleasant once is dead pixels on visit two, and it cannot scroll away because the transcript is the scrolling region, not the page. (3) The pass was instructed not to spend Buzz, and `civitai generate` is the only route to a hero the brand system would accept. The brand statement is carried instead by the header mark, drawn from `brand/icon.svg`'s geometry so it costs no asset request from a sandboxed iframe.
decisions.cost: The store listing carries no NEW art from this pass. Existing icon and cover are untouched and remain valid.

decisions.why: Two independent mechanisms in `parseMarkdown`, both reproduced against the parser at `13f32df`. (a) An indented sub-bullet (`   - Type: LORA`) hit the UL branch, which flushed the open OL — so each numbered row became its own single-item `<ol>` and the browser restarted every one at 1. (b) A blank line between items flushed the list outright, same symptom, different route. A third, smaller one: the source's start number was discarded, so `3. / 4.` renumbered to 1. The model's output was never at fault; the exact string in `lib/markdown.ts`'s own header does not render correctly at base and does at HEAD.

decisions.fork: restyle in place vs move the controls
decisions.chose: move temperature and max-tokens into the Settings dialog; keep the model select on a halved, body-coloured strip
decisions.why: A restyle answers 'too loud' but not 'wrong level' — three power-user knobs were siblings of the conversation itself. The model is NOT a tuning knob: it decides what a reply costs (2-4 Buzz for one identical conversation, measured in `lib/models.ts`) and is a per-question choice, so hiding it would hide a spend decision. Temperature and max-tokens belong beside the system prompt, which is where the app's other tuning already lived.
decisions.cost: `temperature-slider` and `max-tokens-slider` leave the boot DOM for the settings dialog. Neither is named by the capture recipe's `ready`, `clickable` or `states`, and both now appear INSIDE the recipe's existing `settings` state, which is a better shot than before. `settings-bar` and `model-selector` are deliberately unchanged.

It also silently broke the setup of six 🔴 regression tests that create their second session by pressing '+ New' twice (clawgate #425/#427/#434); rewriting those setups would have risked disarming guards for real prior incidents in order to buy a smaller win.

PR #69's priced refusal is unaffected either way (`isTerminalWithoutSuccess('failed')` is `true`, same exit, same message). The prohibition is now ENFORCED rather than advisory: `reports the workflowId for a terminal submit reply that is not failed` in `orchestrator-bridge.test.ts` goes red under the widening — `1 failed | 683 passed (684)`, with `tsc --noEmit` clean — where before it was wholly green. constraintWriteBackNeeded.content: A markdown-ish inline node that carries a STRING where it should carry CHILD SPANS silently swallows every construct nested inside it, and the loss is invisible to a parse-tree test that asserts the string. Measured on sensei 0.1.12: `bold` was `{ kind:'bold'; text:string }`, both bold and link matched at different offsets, the earlier offset won, and every `**[Name](url)**` citation — the app's entire output — rendered as its own raw source. It had shipped that way through twelve releases behind a test NAMED 'renders a bold link' whose expectation pinned the swallowed source verbatim. The general shape: when a renderer's node type has a leaf where the grammar has a container, the defect presents as 'feature X never works' rather than as a crash, and a test written from the observed output freezes it. Check container-ness before believing an inline grammar.
